summary: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima (1927–2017) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Tendzin Lodro Gyatso and earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery. He founded Menri Monastery, serving as its abbot from 1969.
Lungtok Tenpé Nyima studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He later taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

Lutz Bieg (born 1943) is a sinologist who studied at Heidelberg University (Dr. phil., c. 1963–1971) and Freie Universität Berlin (Habilitation, c. 1972–1986). From 1989 to 2008, he served as ordentlicher Professor at the University of Cologne.

Lynn Struve (born 1944) is a scholar of sinology and history. She studied at the University of Washington (c. 1963–1967) and the University of Michigan (c. 1967–1974), and served on the faculty at Indiana University Bloomington (c. 1977–2010).

Lynn Thomas works in Indology and religious studies. She earned degrees from Lancaster University and a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford (until 1987), later serving as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

Léon Feer (1830–1902) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Marc Quatremère and Philippe Édouard Foucaux. He held posts at INALCO (from 1864), Collège de France (1869–1872), and the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1872, 1900).

Sinologist and philosopher Léon Vandermeersch (1928–2021) studied at INALCO, the University of Paris, EPHE, and Paris Diderot. He held posts at Paris Diderot (1973–1979), EPHE (1979–1993), Maison Franco-Japonaise (1981–1984), and directed the EFEO (1989–1993).

Lê Mạnh Thát (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history. He earned a BA at Saigon University (c. 1962–1965) and a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (c. 1967–1974), later holding a post at Vạn Hạnh University (c. 1974–1975).

M. A. Mehendale (1918–2020) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and held professorships at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1970, 1983, and 2026).
M. Athar Ali (1925–1998) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University from c. 1948 to 1953 and served there as a historian from c. 1953 to 1995.

M. D. Balasubrahmanyam, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, completed his dissertation at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested there in 1967). He also served as Reader at Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha and Principal at Rashtriya Sanskrit Sansthan (attested 1973).

M. H. Krishna (1892–1947) studied at Maharaja's College, University of Madras, and University College London under Ernest Arthur Gardner. An Indologist and historian, he served as Professor and dean at the University of Mysore and department head at Maharaja's College.

Philosopher M. M. McCabe (born 1948) studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She was a Fellow at Murray Edwards College (1981–1990), Professor at King's College London (1990–2014), and held posts at UCL and Newnham College.

M. R. Raghava Varier (born 1936) is an Indologist, historian, and linguist. He earned degrees from the University of Calicut, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and studied at the Archaeological Survey of India, later serving as Professor at the University of Calicut (c. 1976–1996).

M. S. A. Rao (1926–1985) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. He held posts at the University of Delhi (c. 1959–1985), Syracuse University, and the University of Pennsylvania.

M. S. Nagaraja Rao (1932–2011) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under M. N. Deshpande, at Mysore, and Pune. He held posts at Karnatak University, the Karnataka State Archaeology Department, and served as Director General of the ASI.

M. Seshagiri Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai, Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (attested 1899), and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University (attested 1899).
M. Shinoda (born 1977) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Shinoda studied under Seiren Matsunami, at Agoura High School (c. 1991–1995), and at the Art Center College of Design (c. 1995–1998).

M. Yamunacharya (born 1898) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Mysore Hiriyanna, Ardeshir Ruttonji Wadia, and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He served as Professor in Philosophy at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

M.L. Pattaratorn Chirapravati (born 1958) studied at Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell universities. She held posts at Silpakorn, Tsukuba, the Asian Art Museum, Sonoma State, California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016), Yale-NUS College (2016), and Nanyang Technological University (2022).
